text: Valley, this is Medic 12 coming to you with a stroke alert. Seventy-one year old female, husband says last known well was 0915. On exam she's got a left facial droop, left arm drifts, left leg holds up fine, and her eyes are deviated to the right. ETA eighteen.
notes: Hailing 'Valley' + 'coming to you' = destination. Unqualified droop = facial 2. 'Left leg holds up fine' = leg 0. Only the LKW is governed by 'husband says'.

text: Crushing substernal chest pain, goes up into his left jaw, started at 0640 while he was shoveling the driveway. Fifty-eight, male. Twelve-lead acquired at 0712, ST elevation in II, III and aVF, transmitting to you now.
notes: 12-lead stated as acquired and being transmitted = done -> ecg.attached true plus its time. ST elevation is a finding, not a complaint.

text: Restrained driver, T-boned at maybe forty miles an hour, heavy intrusion on the passenger side, both front airbags deployed. She's complaining of left hip pain. GCS fifteen.
facts: heavy intrusion on the passenger side
notes: 'Complaining of' is the spelled-out c/o of a medic report -> role medic (guide 4b). complaint.chief is a single string: one fact (MOI 'T-boned' also valid; presence-scored). GCS 15 total gives no gcs_motor and no ACVPU letter (neither stated). Hedged speed has no key.

text: Daughter came by at lunch and found her like this. Right-sided weakness, speech is slurred. Daughter says she talked to her on the phone at nine last night and she sounded completely normal.
notes: 'nine last night' -> '9 pm'. Found by daughter -> onset_witnessed false (family). Vague deficits, no exam -> no RACE items. No sex (pronouns only).

text: County General, Medic 7, we'll be transporting to you, ETA twelve minutes, stand by for full report.
Known COPD'er, tripoding on the edge of the bed, talking in two-word sentences. Resps thirty-two, sats eighty-four on his home two liters. We've got him on CPAP at ten now.
notes: Home 2 L in use and CPAP both mean on_oxygen true (one fact). CPAP 10 is pressure, not litres. COPD is history, not a complaint.

text: D-stick was thirty-eight, we pushed twenty-five grams of D10, recheck is one forty-four and he's coming around, answering questions.
notes: Recheck -> two glucose facts (4b). D10 given by EMS -> no meds.list. 'Coming around, answering questions' is not an ACVPU letter.

text: She was fine, I mean she was totally fine when I left for the gym at six thirty, and when I got home at seven fifteen she was on the bathroom floor, she couldn't get up.
speaker: husband
notes: 7:15 is the found time: neither LKW nor onset. 'Couldn't get up' is not a named deficit -> no stroke.deficits. No complaint: a fall is not stated.

text: Unresponsive on arrival, pinpoint pupils, breathing six a minute. Two of Narcan intranasal, and now he's breathing twelve and cussing at us.
notes: Narcan given by EMS -> intervention, no meds.list. Before/after RR = two facts (recheck rule).

text: It's like an elephant sitting on my chest, it started, I dunno, maybe twenty minutes ago? I took one of my nitroglycerin pills before you guys got here.
speaker: patient
notes: Hedged onset ('I dunno, maybe ... ?') -> no symptom.onset. Own nitro taken before EMS -> meds.list (4b).

text: RACE: face is symmetric, right arm falls straight to the bed, can't lift it at all, right leg drifts, no gaze deviation, and she's globally aphasic, not getting a single word out.
notes: Negative findings get only the RACE 0; positive findings are also deficits.

text: Ground level fall, uh, tripped over the dog and hit her head on the coffee table. Per patient, no loss of consciousness. She's on warfarin for a mechanical valve.
notes: Mechanism counts as complaint. Denied LOC has no key. Med statement is unattributed -> medic.

text: He takes the Humalog with meals and Lantus at bedtime, and he skipped supper tonight 'cause he wasn't feeling good. I found him all sweaty and mumbling around eight thirty.
speaker: wife
notes: Humalog = insulin lispro, Lantus = insulin glargine. Found time is not an onset. 'Mumbling' is not an ACVPU letter.
adjudication: stroke.* keys only for stroke-like presentations (guide §4b): no onset_witnessed for a found-down hypoglycemic patient

text: RACE of six, screens positive for LVO, requesting you activate the stroke team ahead of our arrival.
notes: A RACE total gives no item scores (4b). 'Stroke team' is not a complaint.

text: Sixteen, known asthmatic, hit her ProAir four times in the last hour, no relief. We gave a DuoNeb. Diffuse wheezes, sats ninety-one.
notes: ProAir (albuterol) used by the patient before EMS -> meds.list. DuoNeb given by EMS -> no fact. Asthma is history, no complaint stated.

text: Seventy-nine year old female from Maplewood with a Foley. The nurse there says she spiked to one oh three point six and has been lethargic since this morning. Pressure eighty-four over fifty, heart rate one twenty-two.
notes: Facility nurse -> family. 103.6 F -> 39.8 C, reported by the nurse -> family role. Fever not repeated as a complaint (captured by temp). 'Lethargic' is not an ACVPU letter.
adjudication: a stated presenting problem with no structured key ('lethargic') is complaint.chief (guide §4b)

text: pt is on eliquess for a fib per the son last dose this morning left arm and leg are weak no facial droop
notes: 'eliquess' = Eliquis (ASR). 'per the son' governs the med clause only. 'Weak' is vague -> deficit only, no arm/leg RACE. 'No facial droop' -> facial 0.

text: Gave three twenty-four of aspirin, chewed, and one nitro sublingual. Pressure before the nitro was one fifty-two over ninety, sorry, one thirty-two over ninety.
notes: Aspirin and nitro given by EMS -> no meds.list. BP corrected -> only 132/90.

text: I saw the whole thing, the truck turned left right in front of him and he went flying over the handlebars. No helmet. He was knocked out for like a minute.
speaker: bystander
notes: Mechanism counts as complaint (v1_065). Helmet use treated as an explicit scene observation. LOC has no key.
adjudication: stroke.* keys only for stroke-like presentations: no onset_witnessed for a witnessed bike crash

text: Clearing St. Luke's, back in service.
notes: Clearing a hospital after drop-off is not a transport destination.

text: Aide at the nursing home says she was at her baseline for the two a.m. bed check and they found her like this at six. On our arrival she has a left facial droop and she's not moving the left arm at all.
notes: Facility aide -> family. 'At her baseline' = last known well. Found at six -> unwitnessed (6 is the found time, no key). 'Not moving at all' = no movement -> arm 2.

text: sugar reads four hundred eighty seven kussmaul breathing around thirty fruity breath per mom shes been vomiting since yesterday shes fourteen and on an insulin pump
notes: 'per mom' governs everything after it in the run-on. 'around thirty' is an approximation, kept as 30. Insulin pump -> meds.list ['insulin'] (generic name, no brand given).
adjudication: attribution is clause-scoped in run-ons: 'shes fourteen and on an insulin pump' is a new clause -> medic

text: Per the daughter, cough and fever for three days. Temp's 102.4, resp rate twenty-six, sat eighty-nine percent on room air, and she's confused, which the daughter says is new.
notes: 102.4 F -> 39.1. Duration 'for three days' -> '3 days' (the 'for' dropped). Confusion observed by the medic -> C medic; the daughter only vouches that it is new.

text: Passed out in the pew during the service, people around her say she was out maybe thirty seconds. Denies chest pain beforehand. Takes Toprol and hydrochlorothiazide. Ninety-two over fifty-eight sitting up.
notes: Toprol = metoprolol. 'Ninety-two over fifty-eight' with no 'BP' word is still an X-over-Y BP. Hedged duration has no key. Denied chest pain -> no fact.

text: I wasn't there, but Mrs. Alvarez next door told me she saw Dad getting the mail at ten and he waved and talked to her, totally normal. Then he called me at eleven thirty and his words were all slurred.
speaker: daughter
notes: Nested attribution: neighbor's observation relayed by the daughter -> bystander (4b). 11:30 is when the daughter noticed, not onset. 'Dad' is kinship, not a sex descriptor -> no patient.sex.

text: st elevation mi alert inferior leads pt is 64 yo female diaphoretic and pale bp 88/50 hr 44 were 11 minutes out to st marys cath lab
notes: No 12-lead is mentioned as done or attached -> no ecg keys (not inferred from 'inferior leads'). STEMI alert is not a complaint. 'were' = we're (ASR).

text: He says he was, uh, jumped by two guys outside the bar, got kicked in the ribs a bunch. Denies hitting his head. Breathing's twenty-four and shallow, sats ninety-three.
notes: Mechanism (assault) comes from the patient's account -> patient. 'two guys' is not a spoken vital.

text: Stroke alert, stroke alert. LKW fourteen hundred, correction, thirteen hundred per the wife. Right facial droop, mild, and right arm drift.
notes: Corrected LKW -> only 1300. Mild droop -> 1.

text: Hey, can somebody grab the stair chair out of the rig, and the extra O2 bottle?
notes: Equipment request; 'O2 bottle' does not say the patient is on oxygen.

text: Staff at Oak Hill says she's more confused than her baseline since yesterday morning. Dementia at baseline, normally A and O times one. Temp ninety-nine point one.
notes: Facility staff -> family (v1_039 pattern: 'more confused than baseline' = C, no complaint). Baseline A&O x1 is history, not a current ACVPU. 99.1 F -> 37.3.

text: Roommate thinks he went to bed normal, maybe around midnight, but honestly he's not sure, he got home late himself. Patient woke up with the whole left side not working.
notes: Hedged LKW -> no stroke.lkw. 'Woke up with' -> onset_witnessed false; stated by the medic, unattributed -> medic.

text: Known peanut allergy, ate a cookie at a birthday party, throat feels tight and she's covered in hives. Used her own EpiPen at 1935 before we got here, we just gave a second epi IM.
notes: Her own EpiPen used before EMS arrived = home med taken before arrival (4b nitro rule) -> epinephrine. The second epi IM was given by EMS -> no fact. 1935 is a dose time, not onset.

text: He's on Crestor and lisinopril, and he has the nitro spray but he didn't use it. No blood thinners, the cardiologist took him off the Eliquis last year.
speaker: wife
notes: PRN nitro is on his home med list even though not used today (judgment: 'didn't use it' negates today's dose, not the prescription). Discontinued Eliquis -> not listed. Explicit 'no blood thinners' -> none.

text: Fell, uh, roughly twelve feet off a ladder cleaning gutters, landed flat on his back on the driveway. Fifty-two, male, says he can't feel his feet.
notes: Numbness from a suspected spinal injury is not a stroke deficit -> no stroke.deficits (judgment). Height of fall has no key.
adjudication: stroke.* keys only for stroke-like presentations: spinal numbness after a fall is not stroke.deficits

text: Okay so, uh, face is symmetric, left arm drifts, left leg's fine, eyes are parked to the right, and she doesn't recognize her left arm as her own, but she does know she's weak.
notes: Recognizes the deficit but not the arm -> agnosia 1. 'Parked to the right' = gaze deviation.

text: Orthostatics: heart rate seventy-four lying, one-oh-eight standing, uh, correction, one-eighteen standing.
notes: Two positions = two HR readings (like a recheck); the standing value is corrected 108 -> 118.

text: BGL fifty-three, sorry, thirty-five, I flipped the digits. She's only responding to voice.
wife says hes been sleeping in the recliner cause he cant lay flat and he takes lasics and coreg bp 196/104 sats 86 crackles up to the shoulders
notes: 'lasics' = Lasix (ASR). The wife's clause runs through the meds ('and he takes'); vitals afterward are medic readings.

text: Wife watched it happen at quarter past seven, he was reading the paper and just stopped talking mid-sentence. Now he can't get any words out and the right side's weak.
notes: Clock time of a witnessed onset -> symptom.onset, not LKW (guide 4). 'Can't get any words out' = can't speak -> aphasia 2. 'Weak' is vague -> no arm/leg item.

text: Change of plans, we're diverting to Kaiser Santa Clara, Valley's on CT divert. New ETA twenty-two.
notes: Valley is named only as the hospital on divert, not the destination.

text: Thirty-one year old guy, sharp chest pain that's worse lying flat and better leaning forward, had the flu last week. Temp one hundred point nine, heart rate one oh six, ninety-eight percent on room air.
notes: 'guy' used as a descriptor -> M (judgment). 100.9 F -> 38.3. 'Ninety-eight percent on room air' is SpO2 from context.

text: She fell off the monkey bars, maybe ten minutes ago, and her arm looks bent the wrong way. She's seven. She's allergic to amoxicillin, it gives her a rash.
speaker: mom
notes: 'maybe ten minutes ago' is hedged -> no symptom.onset (convention: 'maybe/I think/not sure' = hedge; 'about/around/like' = approximation that keeps the value).

text: medic 4 to mercy stroke alert 80 year old mail last known well 3:45 pm per caregiver right face droop right arm and leg flaccid glucose 132 eta 9
notes: 'mail' = male (ASR homophone). Caregiver -> family, LKW clause only. Flaccid -> arm 2 and leg 2.

text: He was shaking all over for like two minutes, and his temp was 103.1 when I checked it at home. He's four. He's never had a seizure before, ever.
speaker: mom
notes: Home temp measured by mom -> family. 103.1 F -> 39.5. 'Two minutes' is the seizure's duration, not an onset time. Seizure history has no key.

text: Family thinks he might be diabetic, maybe on some kind of pill for it, but nobody's really sure.
notes: Entirely hedged, and no medication named.

text: He's three. The barky cough started last night around eleven, and he's never had anything like this. No allergies.
speaker: dad
notes: 'last night around eleven' -> '11 pm' (approximation kept). 'No allergies' -> [].

text: She's a little slurred, and she tells me her left hand's felt clumsy since, she thinks, maybe an hour ago, she's not sure exactly.
notes: Two deficit facts with different roles: slurring observed by medic, clumsy hand reported by patient. Hedged onset -> no symptom.onset. Vague -> no RACE.

text: Per the charge nurse at Sunrise, she was found on the floor next to her bed at 0400, unwitnessed. Left leg's shortened and externally rotated. POLST on file says DNR.
notes: stroke.onset_witnessed is reserved for stroke onset; not used for an unwitnessed fall (judgment). No complaint: a fall is implied, not stated. Sunrise is the facility, not the destination. POLST sentence is unattributed -> medic.
adjudication: stroke.* keys only for stroke-like presentations: no onset_witnessed for an unwitnessed fall

text: Denies shortness of breath, denies nausea, pain doesn't radiate, no cardiac history.
notes: Symptom denials give no complaint facts (guide 5).

text: Scene's got an empty bottle of Seroquel and a half-empty Xanax bottle on the nightstand. Boyfriend thinks she took maybe twenty of them, but he honestly doesn't know.
facts: empty Seroquel bottle on the nightstand
notes: Pill bottles are scene observations; they are not stated as her medications -> no meds.list. Hedged ingestion -> no fact.

text: Mom takes Coumadin, the Lipitor, and something for her thyroid, I think it's Synthroid? She's allergic to penicillin.
speaker: son
notes: Hedged Synthroid -> no levothyroxine.

text: dispatch medic 3 show us on scene one patient will advise
notes: 'will' = we'll (ASR).

text: Blood sugar's, um, sixty-one. She's on Glucophage and Jardiance, and her son says she hasn't eaten since Tuesday.
notes: Glucophage = metformin, Jardiance = empagliflozin. The son's statement (not eating) has no key.

text: unit 22 to regional trauma we have a 19 year old female unrestrained rollover ejected bp 86 over 40 heart rate 130 gcs 9 motor 5 eta 6 minutes
notes: GCS 9 total is not a key; motor 5 is stated. Mechanism -> complaint.

text: She won't tolerate anything on her face. Let's see if she'll let us try a nasal cannula in a minute.
notes: Future action -> no vitals.on_oxygen.

text: Repeat stroke exam at 1420: no droop, both arms hold without drift, no leg drift either, gaze midline, following commands and naming objects fine.
notes: All-negative exam: RACE zeros only, no deficits. 1420 is the exam time (no key).

text: pt states the chest pain comes and goes since around four takes lipiter and metoprolol and a baby aspirin every day
notes: 'lipiter' = Lipitor (ASR). 'pt states' governs the whole unpunctuated run-on -> patient. 'around' dropped from the time value.
adjudication: attribution is clause-scoped in run-ons: the subjectless 'takes lipiter...' clause is the medic's

text: Forty-three, no, sorry, thirty-four year old female, right lower quadrant pain since last night, allergic to codeine and latex.
notes: Age corrected 43 -> 34.

text: Single stab wound to the left flank. Bystander says the guy who did it might've had a second knife, not sure if he got stabbed more than once. That's the only wound I can find.
notes: Bystander's hedged statement yields nothing.

text: History of A-fib, and husband says she's on Pradaxa, no, sorry, he's correcting himself, it's Xarelto.
notes: Med correction: only the corrected drug (Xarelto = rivaroxaban). Dabigatran must not appear.

text: were gonna head to good sam eta is like eight minutes
notes: 'like eight' is an approximation -> 8.

text: Eyes open to pain, incomprehensible sounds, localizes, so GCS two, two, five, nine total. Sugar's ninety-eight.
notes: E2 V2 M5 -> motor stated as 5. Eyes open only to pain -> P.
adjudication: words that state the response ('eyes open to pain') give the ACVPU letter P; a bare GCS number does not

text: Sats eighty-nine, I mean ninety-eight, the probe was on her nail polish, now reading ninety-eight on room air. Resps eighteen, unlabored.
notes: 'I mean' -> correction; only 98.

text: Patient states the room's been spinning and she can't walk a straight line for the past two hours. Denies weakness or numbness. Speech sounds normal to me.
notes: Ataxia reported by the patient -> deficit (judgment). Medic's 'speech sounds normal' -> aphasia 0 (findings in words, 4b). 'for the past two hours' -> '2 hours'. Denied weakness/numbness -> nothing.
adjudication: time value kept as spoken ('for the past 2 hours'); the scorer treats it as '2 hours'

text: Let's get her on the monitor, and I'll do a twelve-lead once we're in the truck.
notes: Future 12-lead -> no ecg keys (4b).

text: Memorial, Medic 9, we're twelve out, check that, fifteen minutes out, traffic's backed up on the bridge. Pressure's holding at one oh eight over seventy.
notes: ETA corrected 12 -> 15. Hailed hospital = destination.

text: He's calm, cooperative, sitting on the curb with PD, says he just wants to go home.
notes: Calm/cooperative is not an ACVPU letter.

text: Collapsed at the checkout line about twenty minutes ago per the store manager, witnessed. Gaze is deviated left, right arm's flaccid, and he's grunting, no real words.
notes: Store manager -> bystander. 'about' dropped from the onset value. 'Collapsed' not labeled as a complaint (not an injury mechanism). 'No real words' = cannot speak -> aphasia 2.
adjudication: a stated presenting event ('collapsed') is complaint.chief, like 'fall' (guide §4b)

text: pts now a and o times 4 sugar 112 after the oral glucose wants to refuse transport
notes: Oral glucose given by EMS -> no meds.list.

text: Okay vitals, BP is, um, one-ten over seventy, hang on, cuff slipped, one-forty over eighty-six. Heart rate ninety-two, resps twenty.
notes: Cuff slipped -> first reading invalid -> correction, not a recheck (judgment). Only 140/86.

text: On my count. One, two, three.
notes: Counting is not a measurement.

text: Found at the bottom of the basement stairs, probably fourteen steps, blood on the landing. His wife heard a thump and came running.
facts: found at the bottom of the basement stairs
notes: No complaint: a fall is implied, not stated. Hedged step count has no key.
adjudication: stroke.* keys only for stroke-like presentations: no onset_witnessed for a found-down fall

text: She uses the Spiriva every morning and the rescue inhaler, the albuterol, she's used it like six times today. She quit smoking back in 2019.
speaker: husband
notes: Spiriva = tiotropium.

text: so the wife says he was normal last night went to bed at ten thirty and woke up at 6 with his right side weak and he cant talk right
notes: 'the wife says' governs the whole run-on. Woke up with symptoms -> false. 6 is the wake time, not LKW/onset. Vague -> no RACE.
adjudication: 'last night' adds pm to a spoken time: LKW '10:30 pm'

text: Temp thirty-eight point nine tympanic, heart rate one-ten, resps twenty-four, and she's only responding to voice. Daughter says she's been coughing up green stuff for about four days.
notes: Temp already Celsius. 'for about four days' -> '4 days'.

text: Her husband says she's been nauseated and short of breath since lunch. She tells me the worst part is a pain between her shoulder blades. Seventy-six, diabetic, takes Lantus at night.
notes: Two complaint facts with different roles (husband's history; patient's own statement). Last sentence unattributed -> medic.

text: Mild left facial droop, left arm drifts down in about five seconds, left leg can't come off the bed, eyes midline. BP two oh four over one twelve, pulse sixty-eight and irregular.
facts: left leg can't come off the bed
notes: Drift within 10 s -> arm 1. Can't lift leg against gravity -> leg 2.

text: Neighbor found him down in the backyard, probably out there all night. Core temp ninety-three point two, and he only responds to pain.
notes: 93.2 F -> 34.0. Hedged time down -> nothing. Not a stroke call -> no onset_witnessed.
adjudication: stroke.* keys only for stroke-like presentations: no onset_witnessed for a found-down hypothermic patient

text: Security found him slumped over the wheel in the parking garage. Looks to be in his sixties, no ID on him. He's confused, keeps asking where he is. Sugar twenty-nine.
notes: Estimated age range -> no patient.age.
adjudication: 'no ID on him' is a stated scene observation -> scene.notes; no onset_witnessed (hypoglycemia, not stroke-like)

text: We were headed to Regional, scratch that, family wants her at Mercy since that's where her doctors are, so Mercy it is.
notes: Destination corrected Regional -> Mercy. The medic announces the destination; the family's wish is the reason -> role medic (judgment).

text: Grandma hasn't been right since breakfast. She keeps dropping stuff with her left hand and her mouth looks crooked. She takes Plavix and the metoprolol.
speaker: granddaughter
notes: Plavix is an antiplatelet, not in the anticoagulant list -> no meds.anticoagulant. Lay observation 'mouth looks crooked' -> deficit only, no RACE facial (not an exam finding; judgment). 'Grandma' is kinship, not a sex descriptor.

text: Neighbor says he hit him with Narcan before we got here. Possible overdose, we don't know on what. Resps are ten, sats eighty-eight.
notes: Narcan given by a bystander is an intervention, not the patient's home medication -> no meds.list (contrast v2_032). 'Possible overdose' is hedged -> no complaint.

text: Pelvis is unstable. BP ninety-eight over sixty, I misread that, seventy-eight over sixty. Pulse one twenty-eight and thready.
notes: Misread -> correction; only 78/60.

text: Sudden onset SOB about an hour ago, just flew back from Tokyo. She's on birth control and denies any blood thinners. HR one-eighteen, sats ninety-two on four liters by cannula.
notes: 'Birth control' is a drug class, not a named generic -> no meds.list (judgment). 'denies' -> patient. 'about' dropped from onset.
adjudication: a drug class without a drug name ('birth control') is not meds.list, as with 'something for her thyroid' (v1_050)

text: Pain's an eight out of ten. Gave fifty mics of fentanyl IV at 1510, and I'll repeat the twelve-lead en route.
notes: Pain score has no key; unlocated 'pain' is not a complaint. Fentanyl given by EMS. Future repeat 12-lead -> no ecg keys.

text: black tarry stools for 2 days on zarelto for afib hr 124 bp 90/56 pale and weak
notes: 'zarelto' = Xarelto (ASR).

text: Group home staff say she woke up like this, unwitnessed, and last known well was their bed check at twenty-two hundred. Sats ninety-seven room air, sugar one eighteen.
notes: Group-home staff -> family.

text: i just take the zocor and the blood pressure one norvasc no allergies that i know of
speaker: patient
notes: 'no allergies that I know of' is the standard NKA phrasing -> [] (not treated as a hedge; judgment).

text: His chest started hurting at nine, no wait, eight thirty, he called me right after. He's allergic to sulfa and, um, maybe morphine? I'm not sure about the morphine.
speaker: daughter
notes: Onset time corrected 9 -> 8:30. Hedged morphine allergy excluded.

text: Um, ED, Medic 15, uh, we're, we're about five minutes out with the, uh, the chest pain patient I called in earlier.
notes: 'the chest pain patient' states the complaint (judgment). 'ED' is not a named destination.

text: Um, she's got a, a left, no, a right-sided facial droop, pretty subtle actually, and the right arm is, uh, drifting.
notes: Side corrected left -> right. 'Pretty subtle' = mild -> facial 1.

text: Roofer, out in the sun all day, core temp one oh four point two, sorry, one oh five point two. He's confused and he's stopped sweating.
notes: Corrected 105.2 F -> 40.7 C (104.2 must not appear).

text: Choking on steak at the restaurant, a bystander did the Heimlich and it came out before we arrived. She's talking fine now, sats ninety-nine, lungs clear.
notes: Bystander's Heimlich is an intervention, not a statement.

text: Ped struck at low speed, thrown onto the hood, starred windshield. Sats ninety on room air, now ninety-six on a non-rebreather.
notes: Before/after oxygen: two SpO2 and two on_oxygen facts (recheck rule applied to the O2 state; judgment).

text: He's A and O times four, pale, cool and clammy. Rate's in the forties, forty-two on the monitor, pressure ninety-four over sixty. Pads are on.
notes: 'in the forties' is a range; 42 is the reading -> one HR fact. Pacer pads are not a 12-lead.

text: She's on hospice, she has a DNR, the paper's on the fridge. We just want her comfortable. Her breathing changed about an hour ago.
speaker: son
notes: Location of the paper is the son's statement, not a medic scene observation -> no scene.notes. 'about' dropped.

text: Complete left facial paralysis, left arm and leg are flaccid, head and eyes turned to the right. She insists nothing's wrong with her, though she does know that's her arm.
facts: head and eyes turned to the right
notes: Recognizes the arm but not the deficit -> agnosia 1. 'She insists' describes anosognosia, not a patient-sourced fact.

text: Two-car MVC, restrained driver, seatbelt mark across the lower abdomen, c/o belly pain. His wife was the passenger, second unit has her.
notes: c/o -> medic (4b). One complaint string (MVC also valid; presence-scored). Seatbelt mark is a patient finding, not a scene note.

text: Pulling into the bay now.
NKDA. Takes Eliquis twice a day for a clot in his leg, last dose last night. Full code per his wife.
notes: 'per his wife' governs only the code-status clause.
